name: manual_60e2ca
claim: Never abandon a task midway when switching strategy -- finish or explicitly checkpoint ALL pending sub-tasks first, save every in-process file, and never delete pending work; preserve and build on it unless a human operator's explicit override says to abandon it. Never discard without HITL (human-in-the-loop) confirmation. Carve-out: this does not block immediate quarantine or sanitization of credentials, PII, .env/.env.local files, or other unsafe artifacts discovered mid-task -- retain only sanitized evidence of those, and preserve everything else unless explicitly overridden.

decisions.notes: Same incident: when the user redirected from a commit-by-commit cherry-pick to a synthesized-single-commit approach, the instinct was to tear down the in-progress worktree/branch entirely rather than checkpoint it and continue building on the resolved portions (already-reconciled files like AGENTS.md and App.svelte). The correct behavior, confirmed by the user, was to resume from exactly where the work left off, not restart from scratch -- switching strategy is not the same as abandoning work, and neither should happen without the human explicitly saying so.
